events.description: Bin Ladin and al-Zawahiri's EIJ announced the World Islamic Front for Jihad against the Jews and Crusaders, calling on Muslims to kill Americans
Bin Ladin gave interviews and press conferences to international journalists at Zhawar Kili
Near-simultaneous bombings of two US embassies in Africa by al-Qa`ida operatives
US cruise missile strikes on jihadist training camps around Zhawar Kili
Abu'l-Walid, accompanied by Yuldashev, met Mullah Jalil and Mullah Omar in Kandahar and pledged bay`a by handshake
Late November: Bin Ladin told Abu'l-Walid he would pledge to Mullah Omar but then did not attend; he later had Abu'l-Walid give the bay`a on his behalf
The Taliban ordered several Arab training camps closed and pressure on Bin Ladin increased
Abu Mus`ab al-Suri e-mailed Bin Ladin on behalf of the Taliban urging a personal apology to Mullah Omar
Early 2000: Bin Ladin personally called on Mullah Omar and relations improved
September 2001 attacks, planned by Bin Ladin without informing Mullah Omar; the Taliban regime collapsed afterwards
Abu'l-Walid's account of the Arabs' pledge was posted on jihadist forums (July 19-20, 2007)
Mullah Omar ordered a halt to attacks on Pakistani troops
Mullah Omar's message describing the Taliban as nationalist
Al-Zawahiri's eulogy for Baitullah Mehsud calling nationalism 'Satanic'
Abu'l-Walid begins working for al-Qa`ida as trainer at its Afghan camps.
Al-Qa`ida leadership moves back to Afghanistan from Sudan.
Abu'l-Walid working for the Taliban as co-editor of al-Imarah with Abu Mus`ab al-Suri.
Bin Ladin interviewed by Ahmad Zaydan, referring to Taliban restrictions on external operations.
Bin Ladin begins publicizing his allegiance to Mullah Omar.
Algerian group rebrands as AQIM.
Abu'l-Walid's Qissat al-bay'at al-'arabiya posted on jihadist forums (July 19-20, 2007).
Letter addressed to TTP leaders.
Second intifada begins; Taliban reportedly not opposed to strikes on Israel from their territory.
Bin Ladin, joined by Zawahiri's EIJ, announced the World Islamic Front for Jihad against the Jews and Crusaders, calling to kill Americans.
actors: World Islamic Front for Jihad against the Jews and Crusaders

events.description: Bin Ladin gave interviews and press conferences to international journalists at Zhawar Kili camp complex.
Near-simultaneous bombings of two U.S. embassies in Africa by al-Qa`ida operatives, some trained in Afghan camps.
U.S. cruise missile strikes on jihadist training camps around Zhawar Kili in retaliation for embassy bombings.
Influx of new Arab volunteers into Afghanistan after the embassy bombings; new training camps built; Arab groups opposed Bin Ladin.
Abu'l-Walid proposed to Bin Ladin, Abu Hafs al-Masri and other leaders that Arab groups pledge collective allegiance to Mullah Omar; met with ridicule and objections.
Abu'l-Walid consulted Mullah Jalil, who affirmed anyone in Afghanistan could give bay`a to Mullah Omar.
After the Taliban's fall Abu'l-Walid fled Afghanistan for Iran.
Abu'l-Walid began posting electronic editions of his memoirs.
Abu'l-Walid renewed his relationship with the Taliban's media wing.
Abu'l-Walid learns that al-Qa`ida leaders had reverted to the position that bay`a to Mullah Omar was permissible only for Afghans.
Abu'l-Walid, with Yuldashev, called on Mullah Jalil, then met Mullah Omar at the governor's residence and pledged bay`a by handshake.
Abu'l-Walid reported his successful bay`a at Arabkhayl to Bin Ladin, Abu Hafs and al-Zawahiri and met a hostile response.
In late November Bin Ladin told Abu'l-Walid at the al-Qa`ida guesthouse that he agreed to give bay`a to Mullah Omar.
Bin Ladin failed to attend his appointment with Mullah Omar, then had Abu'l-Walid give the bay`a on his behalf by proxy.
The Taliban ordered several Arab jihadist training camps closed, and pressure grew on Bin Ladin from other foreign militants.
Abu Mus`ab al-Suri e-mailed Bin Ladin on behalf of the Taliban, urging a personal apology to Mullah Omar.
Early in 2000 Bin Ladin made a personal call on Mullah Omar, and relations were relatively improved.
The September 2001 attack was planned by Bin Ladin without Mullah Omar's knowledge; the Taliban regime later collapsed.
Mullah Omar issued a message stressing Taliban nationalism.
Al-Zawahiri delivered a eulogy for Baitullah Mehsud, calling nationalism 'Satanic'.
The Taliban leadership addressed an open letter to the Shanghai Cooperation Conference.
General McChrystal gave a statement to the U.S. House Armed Services Committee on the Taliban and al-Qaeda.
Abu'l-Walid's account of the Arab bay`a to Mullah Omar was posted on jihadist web forums on July 19-20, 2007.
Abu'l-Walid's account of the Arab bay`a to Mullah Omar posted on jihadist forums July 19-20, 2007.
Abu'l-Walid begins working for al-Qa`ida as trainer at its camps in Afghanistan.
Algerian jihadist group re-brands as al-Qa`ida in the Islamic Maghreb.
Fazul Abdullah Muhammad writes autobiography Harb ala'l-Islam, citing Abu'l-Walid's memoirs.
Bin Ladin interviewed by Ahmad Zaydan of al-Jazira, mentioning Taliban restrictions.
Second intifada in Palestine begins; Taliban then not opposed to strikes against Israel from their territory.
Bin Ladin begins publicizing allegiance to Mullah Omar.
Letter addressed to leaders of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan.
Robert Fisk's Independent summary of Zaydan's Bin Ladin biography published.

key_claims: Bin Ladin never personally swore bay`a to Mullah Omar; Abu'l-Walid performed a proxy pledge on his behalf in late 1998, leaving Bin Ladin room to deny or confirm it.
Al-Qa`ida's early relations with the Taliban were contentious; Bin Ladin repeatedly violated Taliban conditions on media contact and attacks on the US.
EIJ under al-Zawahiri and the North African groups were the most opposed to pledging allegiance to Mullah Omar.
Abu'l-Walid alleges the bay`a was an 'outright deception' that diverted Mullah Omar's attention from the 9/11 plot.
The Taliban were divided into pro- and anti-al-Qa`ida factions, with Arab rivals of Bin Ladin having Taliban patrons.
Today's professed allegiance of al-Qa`ida, the Haqqani network and TTP to Mullah Omar is expedient, since they pursue a wider conflict that Mullah Omar condemns.
Abu'l-Walid is a Taliban loyalist, so his claims need caution, although they were published in a Taliban organ.
Abu'l-Walid claims Bin Ladin gave no personal bay`a to Mullah Omar; the pledge was a facade.
Abu'l-Walid was a longtime associate of Jalaluddin Haqqani and edited the Haqqani magazine Manba' al-Jihad.
Abu'l-Walid worked for al-Qa`ida and later the Taliban, co-editing al-Imarah with Abu Mus`ab al-Suri.
Taliban Foreign Ministry opposed hosting Bin Ladin and pushed for restrictions on him.
Taliban restricted external operations from Afghan soil, per Bin Ladin's own 1998 statement.
The 9/11 Commission's claim of a bay'a on arrival in Afghanistan is contradicted by other sources.
Bin Ladin began publicizing allegiance to Omar in April 2001.
